data.name: Vatican & Sistine Chapel: Family-Friendly Private Half-Day Tour
data.description: Explore the world-famous Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel with a private guide and learn about Vatican City and the history of the papacy through its extensive collection of art, archaeology and anthropology artefacts gathered by the Popes over the centuries. On your family-friendly private tour, you will: Enjoy the personalised attention of a private tour guide, who will tailor the tour to your family’s interest, to make it engaging for children and teens; Visit parts of the museums not usually seen including the Egyptian Museum, and the Carriage Museum; Explore the Egyptian gallery, to see well-preserved mummies and learn all about Egyptianfunerals; See the amazing carriagepavilion - which still smells of old leather and horses, see centuries-old carriages used by Popes on ceremonial occasions and old horse liveries and uniforms;  Walk down the halls of busts and statues, filled with ancient statues of gods, heroes, and wealthy Roman men and women, to learn all about life and fashions in ancient Rome; See the famous Laocoön and Apollo statues; Walk the galleries of Candelabras - filled with ancient statues, the Raphael Tapestries, and the dazzling 16th century frescoed Maps; Marvel at the astounding works of Michelangelo Buonarroti as you enter the Sistine Chapel; See if you can find some naughty jokes that Michelangelo hid in his art - that the pope didn't see - but your guide will show you; End the tour inside the Vatican Museums, where you can grab something to eat at one of the family-friendly pizzerias, and keep exploring at your own leisure, or exit the museums with your guide.  Vatican City is the smallest country in the world, yet one of the most culturally rich places on earth! The Vatican Museums are home to some of the world's most admired and valued works of art - many of which are frescos and so immovable - such as the Sistine Chapel. Your private, family-friendly tour will ensure you see all the usual highlights of the Vatican Museums, but also some areas not often seen on guided tours that will really engage your younger family members, such as the Carriage Museum and the Egyptian Gallery. The Carriage Museum still smells of horses and is where you will see a huge array of ceremonial carriages, sedan chairs - and the more modern pope mobiles! The Egyptian museum contains fascinating funereal relics of ancient Egypt - including a well-preserved mummy. You'll also see famous statues such as the Apollo and Laocoön in the Belvedere Courtyard, before walking down the long galleries of the RaphaelTapestries and dazzling Gallery of the Maps. Finally, enter the SistineChapel - the awe-inspiring work of Michelangelo, and perhaps the most remarkable masterpiece in the entire history of art. Your guide will explain the meaning, symbolism, and brilliance of Michelangelo's work, pointing out a few hidden jokes that Michelangelo - who often fought with the pope - left in the frescos! Please note: During the Jubilee Year, Rome is expected to experience increased visitor numbers and heightened security measures. While we strive to provide a seamless experience, some attractions may face last-minute closures without prior notice, longer-than-usual wait times, or time restrictions on visits inside certain attractions due to crowd control policies.In such cases, your guide will expertly adapt the itinerary to ensure the best possible experience, using their local knowledge to navigate any challenges. We appreciate your understanding and patience as we work to make your visit to Rome unforgettable despite these unique circumstances.

data.name: Semi-Private Vatican Tour with Sistine Chapel and St. Peter’s Basilica
data.description: Vatican crowds and long ticket lines can eat up your day and drain the experience. Skip the wait and explore the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel with just 10 guests per group. This semi-private tour offers a more personal experience with a dedicated guide, plus direct entry to St. Peter’s Basilica through the Scala Regia. You’ll end in the basilica, free to explore until you’re ready to take on the rest of Rome.Tour OverviewYou’ll meet your local guide at the top of the stairs near Caffé Vaticano, just across from the Vatican Museums entrance. With skip-the-line access, you’ll head straight inside to explore the treasures of the Vatican without the usual crowds. Your expert guide will lead you through highlights like the Raphael Rooms, Borgia Apartments, and more, sharing the stories behind the art. After your time in the Sistine Chapel, you’ll enter St. Peter’s Basilica through the Scala Regia, where your tour concludes inside one of the most revered churches in the world.Semi-Private Vatican Tour with Sistine Chapel and St. Peter’s Basilica DescriptionYour 3-hour semi-private tour includes:Charismatic, English-speaking guideSkip-the-line Vatican MuseumsPio-ClementinoGalleries, tapestries, maps & moreRaphael Rooms & School of AthensSistine ChapelEnter Scala Regia passagewayMax group size 10Please note that the Basilica is closed on Wednesday mornings due to the Papal Audience and will not be included in tours. Afternoon tours will still include St. Peter's Basilica entry.Pio-Clementino Museum and Nero’s BathtubYour guide will take you to the Pio-Clementino Museum where you'll see three of the most iconic statues in the world. Learn about the myths and legends associated with the Apollo Belvedere, Laocoön and His Sons, and the Belvedere Torso. You'll also visit one of the biggest and oldest bathtubs you'll ever see, made from rare red marble for Emperor Nero to relax in.The Best Galleries at the VaticanYour guide will lead you on through the Vatican Museums, visiting the Candelabra Gallery, Gallery of the Tapestries, and Gallery of Maps. Admire the ancient Roman and Greek statues, the Flemish tapestries created by Raphael's students, and the gorgeous topographical depictions of Italy.At the height of the Roman Empire, pontiffs rarely left Rome. In order to understand the Italian peninsula without endangering his life, Pope Gregory XIII commissioned 40 giant, meticulous maps to be created for his use. Most of these maps measure more than 15 by 16 feet, and the end result is nothing short of spectacular.You'll hear the stories behind these treasures from your expert guide as the Vatican secrets are slowly unveiled to you.Raphael Rooms and The School of AthensRaphael is the epitome of a Renaissance artist. In the period of European civilization immediately following the Middle Ages, a great period of revival in art, literature, and thought occurred. Raphael encompassed the ideals of a Renaissance man and frescoed multiple rooms inside of the Vatican Museums. Among other masterpieces, see one of Raphael’s most famous works of art, The School of Athens.Michelangelo’s Sistine ChapelNo visit to Vatican City is complete without stepping inside the Sistine Chapel. Since speaking is not allowed in this sacred space, your guide will explain the most important details beforehand and provide a helpful reference guide to take in with you.Once inside, the magnitude of Michelangelo’s masterpiece becomes clear. In just four years, he painted over 600 figures across the ceiling and altar wall—scenes from Genesis, prophets, sibyls, and the powerful Last Judgment. The Sistine Chapel is not only a breathtaking artistic achievement, but also the place where cardinals gather to elect a new pope, deepening its spiritual and cultural significance.Please remember that the Sistine Chapel is an active place of worship. Both men and women must cover their knees and shoulders to be granted entry. Rome’s summers can be hot, so we recommend bringing a lightweight shawl or sweater to cover up when needed.Ending Inside St. Peter’s BasilicaAfter your visit to the Sistine Chapel, you’ll follow your guide down the Scala Regia, Bernini’s magnificent ceremonial staircase once used by popes and dignitaries. This route is not open to the general public—only guided groups have access.You’ll step directly into St. Peter’s Basilica, one of the most awe-inspiring churches in the world. Inside, marvel at Michelangelo’s Pietà, gaze up into the dome, and stand beneath Bernini’s bronze Baldachin at the high altar. From here, your guided tour ends, and you are free to explore the basilica at your own pace. Whether you choose to linger longer in the quiet majesty or step back into the streets of Rome, the rest of the day is yours to enjoy.

data.name: The Great Opera Arias Concert at Palazzo Poli
data.description: With a program featuring the great Tosca, Rigoletto, La Traviata and Turandot by Boccherini, Vivaldi, Verdi, Marcello, Puccini, Rossini, Mascagni, Leoncavallo and de Curtis, this opera concert at Rome's beloved Palazzo Poli is sure to set you to return for more. Palazzo Poli is an important sixteenth century palace located in the heart of Rome: It is the palace of the famous Trevi Fountain. The Sala Dante, with its very high ceiling, has excellent acoustics and offers a view of the fountain itself from three balconies accessible to spectators!

data.name: Full-day tour to Florence and Pisa from Rome
data.description: The first stop will be Pisa. Upon arrival, you will go to Piazza dei Miracoli, declared a World Heritage Site and where the Pisan Romanesque-style cathedral is located. In this same square, you will have the opportunity to take the famous photo next to the Leaning Tower of Pisa. After taking the famous picture of the Leaning Tower, you will return to the bus to go to Florence. During the Middle Ages, Florence was an important cultural, economic, and financial center and its streets originated in the second half of the fourteenth century, the Renaissance. The city is replete with history, art, philosophy, and science and there are samples of it in every corner. The tourist leader will take you to a point in the city center and you will have time to make your itinerary and enjoy a city full of curiosities and interesting facts that will allow you to admire Piazza del Duomo, Mercato Nuovo, Piazza della Repubblica or Palazzo Strozzi. You can walk over the Vecchio Bridge and from there reach the Palazzo Vecchio. You will have time to eat on your own and taste the typical Panzanella or Panino col lampredotto.Around 17:30h we will head back to Rome.

data.name: Day trip to Bologna from Rome
data.description: Bologna is home to the oldest university in the Western world, and is known for its lavish porticoed walkways and squares, its fascinating medieval center and its bustling night life. Bologna is also one of Italian food capitals: great pasta such as tagliatelle, lasagne, tortellini as well as delicacies such as Parmesan Cheese, Balsamic Vinegar and some of the finest cured meats in Italy hail from Bologna and the surrounding Emilia Romagna region. All this makes Bologna a perfect off the beaten path destination for the savvy traveler. Wandering under the ancient porticoes and discovering  architectural masterpieces from a long forgotten past (while tasting from time to time local amazing delicacies) could be one of your Italian trip major delights! You will leave Rome in the early morning when our driver will pick up you at your accommodation and you will be back there in the same evening! An expert local guide will stay with you all the time to show all the secrets of this beautiful little treasure in the middle of our country.

data.name: Galleria Borghese: visita guidata in italiano
data.shortDescription:
La Galleria Borghese è tra le gallerie d'arte più famose a Roma. Questo plesso museale ospita una parte consistente della Collezione Borghese di dipinti, sculture e antichità, iniziata dal cardinale Scipione Borghese, nipote di Papa Paolo V e avido collezionista di opere di Caravaggio, che è ben rappresentato nella collezione con il Ragazzo con canestro di frutta, il San Girolamo che scrive, il Bacco malato e altri.

Nota di merito per il meraviglioso Salone: questo, infatti, presenta un grande affresco sul soffitto della prima sala, opera dell'artista siciliano Mariano Rossi, che fa un così buon uso dello scorcio da sembrare quasi tridimensionale. L'affresco raffigura Marco Furio Camillo che allevia l'assedio del Campidoglio da parte dei Galli.

La prima sala del Salone è la Camera di Cerere, con un vaso di marmo raffigurante Edipo e la Sfinge. La seconda sala ha un soffitto affrescato da Francesco Caccianiga con la Caduta di Fetonte. La terza sala ospita l'Apollo e Dafne del Bernini.

Proprio le opere di Gian Lorenzo Bernini, costituiscono una percentuale significativa della sua produzione di scultura profana, a partire dalle prime opere come la Capra Amalthea con Giove bambino e Fauno (1615) e Enea, Anchise e Ascanio (1618-19) fino ai dinamici Ratto di Proserpina (1621-22), Apollo e Dafne (1622-25) e David (1623) , considerati opere seminali della scultura barocca. In Galleria Borghese sono presenti diversi busti-ritratto, tra cui quello di Papa Paolo V e due ritratti di uno dei suoi primi committenti, il cardinale Scipione Borghese (1632).

data.name: The Galleria Borghese Museum: tickets and guided tour in Spanish
data.shortDescription:
The Galleria Borghese is among the most famous art galleries in Rome. This museum complex houses a large part of the Borghese Collection of paintings, sculptures and antiquities, initiated by Cardinal Scipione Borghese, nephew of Pope Paul V and avid collector of works by Caravaggio, who is well represented in the collection with the Boy with Basket of Fruit, Saint Jerome Writing, Sick Bacchus and others.

Note of merit for the marvellous Salone: this, in fact, features a large fresco on the ceiling of the first room, the work of the Sicilian artist Mariano Rossi, who makes such good use of foreshortening that it seems almost three-dimensional. The fresco depicts Marcus Furius Camillus relieving the siege of the Capitol by the Gauls.

The first room of the Salon is the Chamber of Ceres, with a marble vase depicting Oedipus and the Sphinx. The second room has a ceiling frescoed by Francesco Caccianiga with the Fall of Phaeton. The third room houses Bernini's Apollo and Daphne.

It is precisely the works of Gian Lorenzo Bernini that make up a significant percentage of his production of secular sculpture, starting with early works such as the Goat Amalthea with Child Jupiter and Faun (1615) and Aeneas, Anchises and Ascanius (1618-19) up to the dynamic Rape of Proserpine (1621-22), Apollo and Daphne (1622-25) and David (1623) , considered seminal works of Baroque sculpture. In the Galleria Borghese there are several portrait busts, including one of Pope Paul V and two portraits of one of his first patrons, Cardinal Scipione Borghese (1632).

data.name: Rome: Express Pizza-Making Class
data.shortDescription: Learn all the secrets of preparing Italian pizza in one hour!
data.description:
Take part in a fun pizza-making workshop and enjoy an experience that encapsulates the entire tradition of Italian pizza. Just a few steps from the Vatican, you will learn the art of making and baking pizza from scratch, from maser pizza chefs.

Make and eat your own pizza while drinking Roman wine, with the assistance of a professional chef. Cook at your own work station and learn something new. No matter what your level of skill in the kitchen.

Once your hands-on experience has finished, sit down in a cozy restaurant or the outdoor terrace to enjoy the fruits of your labor. No cleanup!

Join our social table, sip wine with your new friends, take the opportunity to ask your Chef all the tips and tricks about Italian food and the best spot to be in Rome.

data.description:
Soak in the sights and listen to an informative audio tour to learn about Rome's unique history and the stories behind its world famous monuments.

Discover the enchanting city of Rome with an authorized hop-on-hop-off route, approved by the Municipality of Rome to ensure the utmost decorum.

Experience the convenience of a strategically located bus stops, all within a comfortable walking distance from the captivating monuments and iconic points of interest that make Rome truly unforgettable.

data.name: Pompeii & Sorrento tour from Rome with Pickup
data.description: Tour duration: Approximately 12 hours. Embark on an unforgettable journey to Sorrento and Pompeii, blending breathtaking coastal beauty with ancient history. Depart from Rome and travel in comfort aboard an air-conditioned coach, passing through the stunning landscapes of the Amalfi Coast. Morning in Sorrento: Upon arrival, enjoy a limoncello tasting at a local producer and uncover the secrets behind this iconic Italian liqueur. Stroll through Sorrento’s charming streets, filled with artisan shops, colorful ceramics, and scenic coastal views. Afternoon in Pompeii: Continue to Pompeii, one of the world’s most extraordinary archaeological sites. Choose from two tour options: Guided Tour: Walk through perfectly preserved streets, temples, and villas with a professional archaeologist who will bring this ancient city back to life. Learn about the catastrophic eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD and how Pompeii remained frozen in time. Audioguide Tour: Enjoy self-paced exploration with a multilingual audioguide, offering detailed insights into Pompeii’s forum, bathhouses, and iconic frescoes. After your tour, relax on the return journey to Rome, arriving in the evening with unforgettable memories of Sorrento’s coastal charm and Pompeii’s timeless ruins

data.name: Rome Jewish Quarter and Trastevere Food Tour with Rooftop
data.description: Your experience begins in the old Jewish Quarter, one of Rome’s best neighborhoods for foodies. First, you’ll sample the famous Jewish-style fried artichokes, which you’ll eat standing up, in the traditional way. Then head to a local bakery to sample an unexpected and delicious sweet treat that represents the Jewish Quarter’s rich cultural heritage.After that, you'll make your way into the historic center (Centro Storico) where you'll pick up your next street food bite: freshly fried codfish from a beloved local hole-in-the-wall, washed down with a glass of wine.Next, at a hidden gem craft beer bar, delve into the world of Roman brewing with a tasting of locally crafted beers, each imbued with distinctive flavors and stories. You'll pair your beers with cold cuts and regional cheeses. Afterwards, you'll cross the Tiber River into Trastevere and indulge in a trapizzino, a delicious fusion between a sandwich and pizza.Finally, as the sun begins to set, you'll follow your guide to a private rooftop for a delightful finale: crafting your own Spritz against the backdrop of Rome's skyline. With panoramic views and a toast to good company, say "cin cin" to an unforgettable culinary journey through the Eternal City.

data.description:
Explore the art of crafting pizza, supplì, and gelato in a hands-on culinary class led by Italian chefs. 

Learn to make traditional pizzas, creamy gelato, and Roman supplì while enjoying bottomless wine to complete your Italian culinary experience.

data.name: Private Rome Evening Walking Tour
data.description: Maximus Tours is proud to offer the most beautiful Private Evening Walking Tour of the Eternal City. See the best of Rome through the eyes of a local, professional guide. Walk the romantic streets at your own pace, ask questions and get unexpected answers. You'll be strolling the city centre from Piazza Venezia to Piazza Navona, the Pantheon, Spanish Steps & finally throw a coin in the Trevi Fountain so you make sure you return. The tour also explores some of the smaller treasures which are off the beaten track and hard to find, but we'll keep these as a surprise. Don't wait until the last minute to book as spaces are limited.

data.name: Semi-private Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel with Reserved Access and meeting point
data.description: Discover the masterpieces of Rome on this tour of the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel. You won't have to worry about waiting in long lines on this tour! We are here to ensure that you skip the lines and our expert guides will be there to give you an insider's point of view. The afternoon tour is the best option to visit the Museums without the morning crowd. The Vatican Museums No trip to Rome is complete without a visit to the Vatican Museums. Home to 54 different galleries including four statue museums: Museo Pio-Clementino, Museo Chiaramonti, Museo Gregoriano Etrusco and the Museo Gregoriano Egiziano. These museums are home to some of the most famous works of art in the world, with artists including: Leonardo Da Vinci, Michelangelo, Caravaggio, Raphael and Giotto, to name a few. An experience that is sure to inspire the art lover in anyone. The Sistine Chapel The 54th gallery of the Vatican Museums is the famed Sistine Chapel. Completed around 1483, the Sistine Chapel is arguably the most famous chapel in the world due to the artwork located within. View many of the most famous frescoes in the world, including the famous ceiling and "The Last Judgement" painted by Michelangelo. Not only does the Sistine Chapel hold some of the world's most precious works of art, it is still used for religious purposes such as the Papal conclave - the process through which a new Pope is chosen. data.name: Underground Rome: Private Catacombs Half-Day Walking Tour
data.description: Discover the underground world of ancient Rome on this exciting, fascinating, and adventurous tour of the Catacombs and the excavated site of Basilica San Clemente. On your private half-day tour you will:  Travel between sites in the comfort of an air-conditioned private vehicle; Explore the hidden underground of ancient Roman burial sites, streets, houses, and temples with an expert private guide; Feel like Indiana Jones or Lara croft as you explore the awe-inspiring subterranean burial chambers and miles of labyrinthine galleries at the Rome Catacombs; Descend below the unique 12th-century basilica of San Clemente and see the archaeological lasagna that is Rome; Walk around a 4th-century church with original 9th-century frescos offering us a glimpse into a long-lost world;  Step down into a mysterious 2nd-century pagan temple to Mithras, and learn about this secretive warrior cult; Walk in the footsteps of the ancient Romans in a 1st-century subterranean Roman house... where one more surprise awaits! Drive just beyond the ancient city walls to visit the labyrinth of underground ancient Christian burial chambers called the Catacombs, then discover the layers and layers of Rome, excavated below the Basilica San Clemente (near the Colosseum): walk through a pagan temple, an ancient roman house, and an early Christian church - all underground! You will often hear historians and locals alike refer to Rome as a lasagna! On this tour, you will literally walk your way through these layers of history, as you discover the different excavated street levels of Rome and the miles and miles of underground graves, dug for and by the ancient Christians two thousand years ago known as the Catacombs. Driving just beyond the Aurelian Wall, you’ll descend into an extensive and complex web of graves; the Christian catacombs. You’ll walk down galleries lined with rectangular empty niches – each one contained a body once. Your guide will explain the different styles of graves, the burial rituals, and funeral rites, decode the extraordinarily well-preserved frescos and symbolic carvings and talk you through the dramatic sacking of the tombs by Barbarians after the fall of Rome. One of the most evocative things about the catacombs is seeing the pick axe marks and scrapes of the fossari (the gravediggers) in the soft tufa rock and the tiny terracotta oil lamps that lit their way as they dug these dark tunnels. It is a truly fascinating, exciting, and humbling experience entering these unique places with your private guide. In the Basilica San Clemente, you’ll learn why Rome was built layer on layer, not in a day but over several hundred years. You’ll learn why so many Christian churches were built on top of pagan temples and hear the stories of the martyrs depicted in frescos in the Middle Ages. Your guide will talk you through a day in the life of an ancient Roman as you walk through a first-century apartment, and explain the initiation rites of the warrior-like cult of Mithras as you gaze into the inner sanctum and see the original altar of Mithras and the bull. This tour ends at the Basilica of San Clemente, located right next to the Roman Colosseum. Please note: the dress code for this tour must be observed (covered knees and shoulders). The catacombs and excavations are chilly and humid at 13 Celsius, so please bring something warm to wear! Also, due to local regulations, during the visit to the Catacombs, you will be part of a larger group. For the rest of the tour, you will be alone with your dedicated private guide. During the Jubilee Year, Rome is expected to experience increased visitor numbers and heightened security measures. While we strive to provide a seamless experience, some attractions may face last-minute closures without prior notice, longer-than-usual wait times, or time restrictions on visits inside certain attractions due to crowd control policies.In such cases, your guide will expertly adapt the itinerary to ensure the best possible experience, using their local knowledge to navigate any challenges. We appreciate your understanding and patience as we work to make your visit to Rome unforgettable despite these unique circumstances.

data.name: Aperitif and Skip-the-Line Ticket for the Vatican Museums
data.description: Enjoy the skip-the-line ticket for the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel combined with a delicious aperitif in the beautiful setting of the Pinecone Courtyard.The Vatican Museums are one of the most prestigious and fascinating cultural destinations in the world. The collections gathered over the years by successive popes offer a unique journey through centuries of art, history and spirituality. Inside the Vatican Museums you can admire works of art by some of the greatest masters in history: the frescoes of the Sistine Chapel, created by the genius of Michelangelo, Raphael Rooms, the Gallery of Maps, the Pio Clementino Museum, the Gregorian Egyptian Museum, the Gregorian Etruscan Museum, the Chiaramonti Museum and the Pinacoteca containing works by artists such as Raphael, Leonardo da Vinci, Giotto and Perugino, just to give some example.Complete your experience with a delicious aperitif at the Pinecone Courtyard. Your aperitif includes: 1 cocktail or soft drinks, still or sparking water, red pizzette, selection of cheeses and cold cuts, Capressin finger, Porchetta di Ariccia with homemade bread, rice, potato croquettes, cous cous à la Méditerranée.Don't miss to admire the other important sculpture in the courtyard: the "Sphere Within Sphere” by Italian sculptor Arnaldo Pomodoro, donated to the Vatican Museums in 1990. Pomodoro’s circular sphere has a mechanism inside that slowly rotates with the wind.

data.name: Chopin & Italian Friends Concerts with Traditional Italian Dinner
data.description: Experience an exceptional evening of piano classics at the impressive Chiesa Evangelica Valdese in Rome, featuring masterpieces by renowned composers such as George Gershwin, Giuseppe Verdi, Frederic Chopin, Giacomo Puccini, Claude Debussy, and Pietro Mascagni. The piano concerts are dedicated to the celebrated Polish composer, Fryderyk Chopin, whose compositions resonate in concert halls worldwide. The pianist will showcase his most famous works during the solo performance, including Impromptu Fantaisie, Preludes, and Scherzo No. 2. Despite only visiting Italy once in Genoa, Chopin's exposure to Italian music and culture in Warsaw influenced his compositions. Alongside Chopin's works, the audience will also enjoy unique arrangements of Italian compositions by composers like G. Verdi, P. Mascagni, and G. Puccini. The exceptional venue of the Waldensian Church in Rome, renowned for its superb acoustics and architectural beauty, further elevates the concert experience. Don't miss this unique opportunity to revel in a piano concert within the grandeur of a church setting. Following the performance, attendees are cordially invited to enjoy a traditional Italian dinner at the nearby Enoteca restaurant, creating a perfect end to the unforgettable evening.

data.name: E-Bike Tour to the Appian Way,  the Aqueduct Park and the Catacombs
data.description: Just outside the historic centre, about 3km from the Colosseum, there is a place you absolutely must visit! data.name: Semi-private Tour of the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel with Pick-up
data.description: Tour duration: 3 hours Embark on a transformative journey through the Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel, and St. Peter’s Basilica, where the nexus of art, history, and spirituality offers an unparalleled experience. This exclusive small-group tour grants you a privileged pathway into the heart of Vatican City, bypassing the ubiquitous crowds with reserved access that leads you directly into a realm of artistic and historical magnificence. Your adventure begins at the Vatican Museums, a treasure trove of art spanning several millennia. With over 54 galleries, including the Museo Pio Clementino, Museo Chiaramonti, Museo Gregoriano Etrusco, and Museo Gregoriano-Egizio, the Vatican Museums house a staggering collection of works. Under the guidance of an expert, delve into the stories behind the ancient statues, ethereal paintings, and intricate tapestries that define the collections. Each hall and gallery unfolds like a book, narrating the tale of human creativity across ages. A highlight of your tour is the Sistine Chapel, an iconic symbol of the Renaissance’s artistic achievement. Stand beneath Michelangelo’s The Last Judgment and the mesmerizing ceiling frescoes, where biblical stories are brought to life with unprecedented vigour and emotion. This sacred space, where popes are elected, resonates with the genius of Michelangelo, enveloping you in a sense of awe and wonder. Journey through the Raphael Rooms, where the Renaissance master Raphael Sanzio da Urbino adorned the walls with some of the most sublime frescoes in the world. Your guide will reveal the intricate details and hidden narratives within these works, including the famous School of Athens, showcasing Raphael’s ability to merge classical philosophy with High Renaissance artistry. The tour affords a special privilege rarely extended to the general public - a direct passage from the Sistine Chapel to St. Peter’s Basilica. This exclusive route allows you to transition seamlessly from the artistic to the spiritual heart of Vatican City. Inside St. Peter’s, you will encounter the pinnacle of Renaissance architecture. Marvel at Michelangelo’s Pietà, Bernini’s Baldachin, and the awe-inspiring dome, each element a testament to the basilica’s enduring beauty and significance. As you traverse the sacred spaces and galleries, your guide will provide insights into the Vatican’s pivotal role in history, the intricate processes of art creation, and the stories of ambition, faith, and power that shaped these masterpieces. This tour not only highlights the artistic achievements of legendary figures such as Leonardo da Vinci, Caravaggio, Giotto, Raphael, and Michelangelo but also offers a window into the cultural and spiritual narratives that have influenced humanity throughout the centuries. Embark on this exclusive tour to discover the wonders of the Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel, and St. Peter’s Basilica in a truly immersive way. Book now to secure your place on this unforgettable journey through art, history, and spirituality, ensuring memories that will last a lifetime. data.name: Churches of Rome: A Tour of Sacred Beauty
data.description:
Rome is deeply intertwined with Catholic faith and history, home to over 900 churches. While it’s impossible to visit them all, our walking tour is the perfect way to start uncovering these stunning treasures.

Join us on a relaxed yet immersive walking tour where you’ll discover some of Rome’s most beautiful churches that many visitors miss. You’ll explore Church of St. Louis of the French, home to priceless Caravaggio masterpieces, and Chiesa di Sant'Agnese in Agone, a gem of Baroque architecture.

Not only will you experience the mouthwatering flavors of Rome, but you’ll also discover the process, meet the makers, and truly understand why Roman Cuisine is considered one of the best in the world.

data.name: Oratorio Del Gonfalone: Love of a poet
data.description: Nestled in the heart of Rome, the enchanting Oratorio del Gonfalone presents an evening of musical romance with 'Amor di poeta'. This captivating event invites visitors to explore the emotive depth of love through the profound compositions of Robert Schumann's Dichterliebe op. 48. The venue, renowned for its stunning Renaissance frescoes, offers a fitting backdrop for this evocative performance, where the power of poetry and music intertwine. 'Amor di poeta' is a concert scene that interweaves music and words in a theatrical approach. The performance explores Robert Schumann's Dichterliebe (Poet's Love), a cycle of Lieder celebrating love, hope, sorrow and death, on texts by Heinrich Heine. Through the figure of the translator, musician and playwright, the scene offers multiple levels of interpretation, engaging the audience in an experience that goes beyond the musical performance, creating a deep connection between Romantic music and reflection on its interpretation.

data.name: The unconventional Ancient Rome
data.shortDescription:
The Unconventional Ancient Rome and Colosseum Private Tour allows you to explore the best of Ancient Rome.

We will visit the Colosseum in a completely new way, walking right on the arena where gladiators fought.

We will walk on the Palatine Hill and see the House of Augustus, the Horti Farnesorum, the gardens of the Pope built on top of the ruins of imperial palaces and, last but not list, the ruins of the Tiberio Palace, reopened after 50 years of restorations.

We will visit the entire Roman Forum, with the Church of Sant Maria Antiqua, the Rampa Domitianae and the Temple of Julius Caesar.

We will end by taking a real walk in the Imperial Forums!

The itinerary and duration of your trip can be completely customized according to your needs and desires.
Of course you will visit the Colosseum skipping the annoying entrance line.

Let us know what you want to do and see and we will plan for you a unique journey into the past.

data.name: Da Roma: tour giornaliero a Pompei
data.shortDescription:
Raggiungi in soli 30 minuti il sito archeologico di Pompei. Scendi all'ingresso principale degli scavi ed evita la coda utilizzando il voucher salta fila. 

 

Cosa ti aspetta:

  • Esplora gli Scavi di Pompei in autonomia 
  • Salta  lunga fila all'ingresso del sito 
  • Osserva come vivevano gli abitanti dell'antica città Romana

 

Inizia il tuo tour dal centro di Napoli, dall'Aeroporto Internazionale o dalla Stazione Centrale. Dopo circa 30 minuti di tragitto , sarai lasciato nelle prossimità dell'ingresso prinicipale delle rovine. Potrai usufruire dell'ingresso salta fila mostrando il voucher e avrai  3 ore di tempo libero alla scoperta del sito passeggiando in piena autonomia. Viaggia indietro nel passato ed immagina la vita durante l'Impero Romano. Passeggia tra le strade acciottolate costruite più di 2000 anni fa e ammira ciò che resta dei negozi , templi e teatri che vennero ricoperti da lava e ceneri durante l'eruzione del vulcano Vesuvio nel 79 AD. Osserva le piastrelle mosaicate delle lussuose ville dei ricchi mercanti che trovarono la loro fortuna nella prosperosa città. Ammira le Rovine della Dimora del Fauno e scopri come si intrattenevano gli abitanti del luogo tra terme, case di incontri e molto altro.

Incluso :

  • Prelievo da Napoli Centro, Aeroporto Internazionale o Stazione Centrale
  • Transfer di andata e ritorno
  • Biglietto d'ingresso prioritario per Pompei

 

Non è incluso :

  • Guida / audioguida

data.name: Rome Private Vespa Tour with Hotel Pickup
data.description: Vespas have long been associated with Rome, but driving yourself can be risky if you’re not experienced with scooters or Roman roads. This tour gets you on the back of a Vespa safely, with a driver/guide to show you around and take control of the gears. As an added bonus, you’ll take home souvenir photos of your experience.

data.name: Rome Half-Day Private Pizza, Wine, Gelato Sightseeing Tour
data.description: Make the most of your time in Rome and experience its history, culture, and cuisine in one half-day private tour. Meet your guide near the Colosseum and walk around to see major landmarks including the Pantheon, Spanish Steps, and Trevi Fountain. Along the way, enjoy delicious slices of pizza with wine, topped off with gelato.

data.name: Rome Pizza Making Class with Italian Chef and Gourmet Toppings
data.description: Master the art of Roman pizza-making with a hands-on class led by an Italian chef in the heart of Rome. Craft authentic dough, simmer vibrant sauces, and customize your pizza with gourmet toppings for a personal twist. Enjoy a uniquely Roman culinary experience in a welcoming, relaxed setting.

data.name: Exclusive Colosseum Arena Floor and Ancient Rome guided tour
data.description: Step into the Arena and live this unique experience in the Colosseum. Book this guided tour at a special price, with skip the line tickets and English-speaking guide. The guided tour also includes the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill.

data.name: Semi private half day in Pompeii from Rome extraordinary afternoon opening
data.description: Explore the ruins of the ancient city of Pompeii on a day trip from Rome. Skip the hassle of navigating train and bus schedules on your own and enjoy semi-private transportation directly from Rome to Pompeii. You’ll explore the remarkably intact city of Pompeii, nearly perfectly preserved by volcanic ash and lava when Mount Vesuvius erupted in 79 AD, with an archeologist guide and learn about the history and culture of ancient Rome. You will leave big urban centers, impressive buildings and modern buildings to cross the countryside characterized by fantastic relaxing landscapes and cultivated fields. Reach the famous Campania Felix, the region of happiness famous for the sun, the sea and pizza, you will visit a small village and from here a hill that until 500 centuries ago was still covered with lava and concealed a secret lasted years: Pompeii 2000 years ago. Are you ready to discover how modern our ancestors were? How their cities were well structured? how do their homes have every comfort? Pompeii is still there, frozen in time and with this tour we will bring it back to their life

data.name: Rome: Pasta Making and Tiramisù Cooking Class
data.description: Held either in a 17th Century Palazzo near Piazza Navona or just steps away from the Pantheon, this interactive class is led by an enthusiastic English-speaking chef. Perfect for kids and adults, locals and visitors, this class is designed for anyone with a passion for delicious food, having fun, and learning something new.Compose creamy layers of bitter-sweet flavor in traditional tiramisù. You will start by assembling scrumptious layers of smooth cream, rich coffee, and sweet cocoa.While the tiramisù settles, you will mix, kneed, and roll out our fresh handmade pasta before infusing it with our favorite seasonal flavors. Vibrant pumpkin tortellini in the autumn, light coils of fettuccine dressed in eggplant in the summer, and succulent ravioli dumplings stuffed with rich, creamy ricotta di pecora… well, essentially any time of the year! Sprinkle on a selection of sumptuous Italian cheeses and your mouth-watering meal is ready to be eaten! Celebrate with friendly, festive company and a perfect selection of red and white wines and soft drinks.

data.name: Rome Baroque Fountains and Squares Private Walking Tour
data.description: Rome has some seriously spectacular fountains and piazzas, and while wandering between spots is the most charming way to explore, it's also the easiest way to get lost. Stay on track while immersing yourself in Roman history on a private tour, which wraps up with an included meal at a local restaurant.

data.name: Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel Private Night Tour
data.description: Skip Rome's crushing daytime crowds with this exclusive after-dark Vatican tour. Your private, English-speaking guide provides skip-the-line access to 54 museum rooms, Raphael's Rooms, Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel frescoes, and more, including the narrow passageways to the Borgia Apartments. You'll experience Renaissance masterpieces in a peaceful evening atmosphere without the tourist chaos—a rare experience in Rome.

data.name: VIP Experience Private Transfer from Fiumicino Airport to Rome
data.description: Traveling has never been so comfortable. A journey is not just a transfer from one place to another, but it is an experience. For that reason nothing is left to chance. A driver will be waiting for you inside the Terminal to monitor your flight before you leave, to make sure you can avoid any inconvenience. After comfortably passing the checks you will see him waiting for you with a sign with your name written on top so you can easily recognize him. After collecting the luggages, pass through the sliding glass door. You will find your driver at the arrival terminal. At this point he will take care of you and your personal effects, you will just have to sit in a luxury Mercedes vehicle, where you can find a bottle of water and a map of Rome. From this moment, Rome is in your hands and if you choose the tour option, the driver will stop in front of all the iconic places of the city and will explain some little anecdote and a bit of history to make you feel like you're no longer a foreigner but a local friend.

data.name: Modern Italian Dinner Near the Vatican
data.description:
Join the latest culinary trend of immersive and social dining where local hosts invite you into their homes for a magical meal.

Join Chef Debora for a culinary journey and wine pairing, through the different regions of Italy. Take a seat at her table and enjoy a refined 4-course menu prepared with fresh ingredients from the farmers' market! The menu depends on the season and on the products availability; the wines will be chosen accordingly to the specific dishes of the night. You can't miss it out!

data.name: Rome Private Cascata Delle Marmore Day Trip
data.description: Visiting Cascata Delle Marmore, one of the highest artificial waterfalls in the world, can be a challenge if you don't have a car. This private tour makes getting to the fall—which was created over 2,000 years ago—a breeze, thanks to private transportation and the services of an English-speaking guide.

data.name: Vatican Museums Sistine Chapel Skip-the-Line Hosted Entrance
data.description: Waiting in admission lines in Rome can be daunting, especially during summer when crowds swell and temperatures soar. With this prebooked ticket, save time by skipping admission lines with an escorted entrance to the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel, among the most visited—and crowded—attractions in the world.

data.name: Rome by Night: Romantic Private Tour (Hotel Transfers Option)
data.description: The Eternal City comes into its own at night, when the crowds die down and lights sparkle across Rome. Feel the romance on this private tour, just for you and your beloved, as you soak up rooftop views, sip prosecco, wine, or a soft drink on Janiculum Hill, and pose for photos with icons including the Colosseum. Upgrade for an even more relaxing experience, with round-trip hotel transfers.

data.name: Vatican Museums Small-Group Tour with Skip-the-Line Entry
data.description: The Vatican Museums can be intimidating for first-time visitors, both for the wealth of its art and for the vast area it covers. With this small-group tour, see the highlights with a guide for a comprehensive introduction to the Vatican Museums, Raphael Rooms, and Sistine Chapel that won’t overwhelm. Plus, skip-the-line entry ensures getting inside is quick and as easy as can be.

data.name: Florence Castel Sant'Angelo Private Skip-the-Line Guided Tour
data.description:
Make your way to Castel Sant’Angelo to meet your private guide in time for a 3pm departure. Then, set out to discover the mighty fortress of Castel Sant' Angelo. With skip-the-line entrance tickets, you'll breeze past the long lines at the entrance and head straight in.

The ancient site was built in 139AD to house the tomb of Emperor Hadrian. Many of his successors were also buried here. It was later converted to a castle in the 14th century.

Learn about its fascinating history as a one-time castle, refuge, prison, and site of public executions from your guide as you explore the ruins, admire sculptures by Bernini, Raggi and Morelli, and walk in the footsteps of former Popes as you visit the papal apartments. Then, and head straight to the star attraction – the grand mausoleum of Emperor Hadrian.

Finally, enjoy a spectacular view over Rome from the castle's panoramic terrace.

data.name: Rome: Santa Maria Maggiore & Liberian Museum Small-Group Tour
data.description: Discover the chuch where late Pope Francis chose to be entombed on this small-group tour of the Basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore and the adjacent Liberian Historical Museum of religious art. Learn about the history of this papal basilica from your guide as you admire highlights including the Loggia of Blessings, Hall of Popes, and Bernini Staircase. End with a guided stroll through the museum to touch on its most important artworks.

data.name: Fast Track - Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel & Raphael rooms
data.description:
Meet your guide at the designated tour office and enter the Vatican Museums with a skip-the-line ticket, bypassing the usual queues. Inside, marvel at one of the world’s largest collections of Renaissance and Baroque art, assembled by various popes over centuries. Listen as your guide unveils stories of powerful pontiffs, controversies, and the rich history behind masterworks such as the frescoes in Raphael’s Rooms—take note of The School of Athens, where Raphael cleverly included portraits of Michelangelo and himself.

Stroll through ornate galleries like the Gallery of the Masks and the Gallery of the Maps, then step into the revered Sistine Chapel. Once reserved for the pope’s private worship, this sacred space is now world-famous for Michelangelo’s transcendent frescoes, The Creation of Adam and The Last Judgement. It’s the perfect capstone to a journey through the Vatican’s unparalleled artistic trove.

data.name: Rome Private Skip-the-Line Vatican Tour
data.description: Specially suited for travelers short on time, this private skip-the-line tour of the Vatican Museums covers top sights in the iconic papal collections in just a few hours. Admire world-renowned masterpieces, from the iconic painted ceiling of the Sistine Chapel to the Raphael Rooms and the Galleries of Tapestries and Maps. Pre-booked, no-wait admission tickets let you breeze past the entrance lines, saving time for taking in the sights.

data.name: Pantheon Fast-Track Ticket with Audio Guide App
data.description: Skip the line and step into the Pantheon’s timeless grandeur with an audio guide app and fast-track ticket. With towering Corinthian columns and its famous oculus casting light from above, this self-paced audio tour unveils the secrets behind one of Rome’s most remarkable architectural feats. Hear the stories of emperors, artists, and engineers who left their mark on this ancient wonder.

data.name: Rome Private Naples Pizza Class by High-Speed Train
data.description: Take a high-speed train from Rome to Naples, the birthplace of pizza, for a private pizza-making class with a master pizza maker. Learn the secrets behind authentic Neapolitan pizza dough in a UNESCO-recognized "Pizza Lab," then bake your own creation in a traditional wood-fired oven. Afterward, enjoy a delicious true Neapolitan pizza with wine while taking in stunning views of Naples' waterfront, Mount Vesuvius, and Castel dell'Ovo.

data.name: Amalfi Coast and Positano Day Trip From Rome With Cruise
data.description: Discover the highlights of the Amalfi Coast without the hassle of organizing an itinerary or hiring a car on this full-day trip from Rome. Relax onboard a comfortable, air-conditioned coach with Wi-Fi, and soak up the scenery as you head out to the coast. Explore the charming towns of Positano and Amalfi, sip limoncello, and hop aboard a boat cruise in Salerno to take in the beautiful views from a vantage point on the water.

data.name: Hadrian’s Villa and Villa d’Este Private Photo Tour from Rome
data.description: Escape the bustle of Rome and discover two spectacular photography destinations with this full-day private photography workshop. Set off from Rome with your professional photographer guide to visit Hadrian’s Villa and Villa d’Este (entrance fees extra) in Tivoli. Capture the ancient ruins and lush gardens, with the assistance of your guide, so you come away with unforgettable shots and improved photo taking skills.

data.name: Sunset Rome Food & Wine Tour around Prati District
data.description: Experience Rome like a local on this mouthwatering evening tour of the Prati District. Stroll through charming streets with a knowledgeable guide, sampling cured meats, cheeses, and unforgettable pizza from hidden culinary gems. Meet passionate artisans who share their recipes and food-making secrets. With groups capped at 13, this intimate tour fills quickly—reserve early.

data.name: Rome to Designer Outlet Castel Romano: Private Transfer
data.description: Don’t waste your precious vacation time waiting for a bus or dragging your shopping bags through the Rome Metro. Instead, let a driver handle all your transfer needs while you relax in a car that’s just for you. Get between your city hotel and the Designer Outlet Castel Romano with ease, thanks to a driver who knows the route like the back of their hand.

data.name: Castel Sant’Angelo Skip-the-Line Ticket with Audio Guide & Gelato
data.description:
Avoid the crowds and make the most of your visit with this convenient and enriching experience. Your ticket includes skip-the-line access to the museum, allowing you to enter smoothly without the hassle of waiting in long queues.

Explore at your own pace with an optional premium audio guide created by expert historians, designed to give you deep insights, engaging stories, and cultural context that bring the artworks to life.

To sweeten the experience, enjoy a complimentary gelato at one of the best ice cream shops near the museum—perfect for a refreshing break after your visit.

data.name: Caravaggio's Art and Life Private Walking Tour in Rome
data.description: Get an in-depth look into the life and legacy of Italy’s first Baroque master on a Caravaggio tour of Rome. Visit several churches in the heart of the city to admire the painter’s original, groundbreaking work, learning the background of each piece and what sets it apart from Renaissance styles. Feel free to ask all the questions you like on the private tour, led by a professional art historian guide.

data.name: Private transfer from Ciampino Airport to hotel in Rome
data.description: Book this comfortable private transfer by luxury Mercedes-Benz from Ciampino Airport to hotel or other accommodations located within the Aurelian Walls of Rome, and start your vacation or business trip in style. An experienced driver will be waiting in the arrival’s hall with a sign with your name on it for ease of contact. There’s no need to worry about flight or customs delays as the driver will wait up to 1.5 hours without extra charge. Then, sit back and relax as they navigate the busy and unfamliar roads to quickly get you to your hotel. Forget the stress of finding a taxi on arrival, or dealing with the public transportation system. The service is available from 7am to 8pm.

data.name: Rome Best of Tour of Trevi Fountain, Pantheon & Spanish Steps
data.description: Join this 90-minute stroll through the very heart of Rome. Delight in the majesty of the Spanish Steps, toss a coin into the iconic Trevi Fountain, marvel at the timeless beauty of the Pantheon, and so much more. With an expert local guide, you'll be transported through centuries of history and culture in the blink of an eye. Prepare to be captivated by the true essence of Rome on this once-in-a-lifetime tour.

data.name: Colosseum St Clements Underground & Crypts for Families
data.description: Explore the Colosseum and the lesser-known Saint Clement’s Church during this archaeologist-led, two-for-one guided tour, specially tailored to families with kids. Visit four underground levels of the fresco-filled basilica, including the ruins of an ancient temple. Colosseum admission is included.

data.name: Vatican Museums with St. Peter’s Basilica small group tour
data.description: Embark on guided walking tour of the Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel, and St. Peter's Basilica with a small group of up to 20 people. With priority access, you can delve straight into exploring these historic sites. Discover fascinating tales about the characters that walked these corridors. Your guide will escort you to the Vatican Gardens balcony for your initial view of St. Peter's Basilica's majestic dome before strolling through the Pinecone Courtyard, home to ancient statues and contemporary sculptures.To reach the Chapel, your guide will navigate you along the Hall of Maps, through the Gallery of Tapestries and into the Gallery of Candelabra. These masterpieces will spring to life as you listen to your guide's commentary via your dedicated audio earpiece. At the Sistine Chapel, take a moment to appreciate the intricate details adorning the walls and ceilings.After immersing yourself in the chapel's rich Renaissance history, use your skip-the-line access to enter St. Peter's Basilica. Here, you'll encounter Michelangelo's Pietá, a poignant depiction of Mary. After this, feel free to linger inside St. Peter's Basilica to further explore this awe-inspiring church or step outside to St. Peter's Square to admire Bernini's optical illusion and the Basilica's façade.In just a span of three hours, you'll be introduced to the artistic treasures of the Vatican in a relaxed and enjoyable way.

data.name: Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine Hill from Rome
data.description: After pick up at your hotel (in selected hotels in central Rome), you will reach the Archeological area with no stress, ready to get the most complete tour of the Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine Hill. Access the Palatine Hill with no line and discover the hill where Rome was founded. Then reach the Colosseum and be blown away by this monument that is the symbol of Rome across the world. The Amphitheater created to entertain ancient Roman citizens with bloody shows of gladiators, animals and cruel games, is now one of the most fascinating landmarks of the City. Then, walk on the original path of ancient Rome along the Via Sacra and see the Temples of Vesta, Antonino and Faustina, the ancient Basilica Julia and Aemilia and dream about the glorious past of the Roman Empire. Truly an unforgettable day!

data.name: Vatican Museums Private Tour
data.description: The only museum that includes others museums. Inside you will find in fact: the Vatican Art Gallery, the Gregorian Egyptian Museum and the Gregorian Etruscan Museum, the Vatican Historical Museum, Gallery of Candelabra and Gallery of Maps. These are only some examples of its incredible variety. If you want to access one of the places that most represents Rome's art patrimony, you can't absolutely miss this tour. Walking tour locations: Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel. A great symbol of Catholic church and of Italy in itself. Well-known around the globe, it attracts every day millions of visitors. Its Museums are the most eminent representation of the art collections accumulated by all the popes through the centuries. The splendor of the Vatican Museums is due to its limitless artistic beauty without equals in the world. It would take a whole day to admire and appreciate every detail of all its works of art: paintings, frescoes, statues, tapestries that give testimony of our history.

data.name: Rome to Florence, Venice, and Sorrento 10-Night Italy Tour
data.description: Want to explore without having to plan a thing or worry about driving? Check off many of Italy's highlights on this multi-day tour from Rome, which takes care of all the details for you. Visit some of the most popular destinations in the country, from Tuscany and Assisi to Venice, Capri, and UNESCO World Heritage-listed Pompeii. Travel hassle-free with accommodation at 3- or 4-star hotels included throughout the trip, plus many meals.

data.name: Skip the Line Vatican Museums with Sistine Chapel
data.description: Avoid wasting time during your Vatican visit on this Vatican Museums and St. Peter's Basilica tour at the no-wait access entrance. Join a knowledgeable guide to pass right by the long entrance queues and start touring the massive museums. See the incomparable Raphael's Rooms, Michelangelo's stunning Sistine Chapel, as well as other museum highlights like the Maps Gallery and Tapestries Gallery. Then visit the impressive St. Peter's Basilica next door.

data.name: Vatican: Quick Access Skip the Line Museums and Sistine Chapel
data.description: Book now to experience the Vatican's top treasures with zero wait! Our Skip-the-Line ticket offers fast-track entry, allowing you to dive right into the Vatican Museums’ rich galleries, without losing time in long lines. Explore the grandeur of the Raphael Rooms, marvel at intricate ancient sculptures, and finish with the Sistine Chapel’s awe-inspiring ceiling, painted by Michelangelo. With this ticket, you'll have the freedom to explore at your own pace while enjoying priority access to some of the world’s most famous masterpieces. Don’t miss this chance to save time and fully enjoy the Vatican's incredible heritage!

data.name: Colosseum Skip-The-Lines Guided Tour for Kids and Families
data.description: Navigate ancient Rome, touring it uniquely in the company of a small group and a tour guide, providing you with a semi-private guided experience. Skip the lines with fast-access tickets and explore the Colosseum, Palatine Hill, and Roman Forum alongside an expert, licensed tour guide. Over a fascinating walk, immerse yourself in the captivating stories of Roman glory and drama while uncovering the rich history and lifestyle of this remarkable civilization. Step into the past with unmatched convenience and expertise.

data.name: Pompeii, Amalfi Coast, Positano Day Tour from Rome
data.description:
Begin your day at Piazzale Flaminio in Rome, where you’ll board a comfortable, air-conditioned bus bound for the ancient ruins of Pompeii—a journey of roughly three and a half hours. Upon arriving at the archaeological site, join an expert guide (an archaeologist) for an in-depth look at the city buried by Mount Vesuvius, admiring centuries-old structures and artifacts preserved by volcanic ash.

Afterward, return to your bus for a scenic drive along the famed Amalfi Coast, arriving at Positano. Stroll the narrow lanes of this charming seaside town, perhaps stopping to sample local cuisine (at your own expense). Then, reboard your bus and head back to Rome, taking with you lasting memories of southern Italy’s rich history and natural beauty.

data.name: Villa Borghese Gardens by Golf Cart
data.shortDescription: Rent a golf cart and explore the Villa Borghese gardens
data.description:
Walking's great, but wouldn't you prefer to explore the stunning greenery of Villa Borghese Gardens in an electric golf buggy? Of course, you would! 

Move at comfortable, non-threatening speeds as you roll gently around 80 hectares of lush landscape garden near the famous Borghese Gallery (inaccessible by golf buggy... for now).

data.name: Ancient Roman Baths & Michelangelo’s Renaissance Basilica in Rome
data.description:
Experience the grandeur of Rome on an exclusive tour through the Baths of Diocletian and the Basilica of St. Mary of the Angels & Martyrs, designed by Michelangelo. Discover Renaissance elegance intertwined with ancient ruins and witness the intricate meridian line and astronomical clock inside the basilica. This journey blends history, art, and science in a setting where ancient engineering meets Renaissance design. Opt for a small group or private tour. For an even richer experience, add a visit to Palazzo Massimo, home to some of Rome's finest ancient art and mesmerising frescoes.

Please note that the itinerary may vary. Depending on the schedule, you may begin your visit at the Baths of Diocletian and proceed to the Basilica of St. Mary of the Angels & Martyrs, or vice versa

data.name: Rome: Private Driving Tour of the Most-Important Highlights
data.description: Check off 10 of Rome's most-important landmarks in just one day on this private driving tour. Journey around the city, from the Pantheon to Piazza Navona and St. Peter's Basilica, and, with insights from your guide, see the history of Rome unfold through its architecture, from the ancient Colosseum to baroque Trevi Fountain.

data.name: Rome Handmade Pasta and Carbonara Small-Group Cooking Class
data.description: It’s hard to think of an Italian dish that’s treated as badly outside its home territory as carbonara. Get to the heart of Italy’s traditions as you make your own pasta and prepare an authentic Italian carbonara, with guanciale not pancetta, pecorino Romano not Parmesan, and definitely no cream or bacon. For added authenticity, enjoy an aperitivo with wine and snacks, plus wine as you sit down to your meal.

data.name: Rome's Charm Exclusive Private Chauffeur Tour
data.description: Experience the timeless charm of Rome in style with an exclusive private chauffeur tour. Visit top landmarks in the city like the Colosseum, St. Peter's Square, and the Trevi Fountain with ease. Discover history and culture along the legendary Appian Way, all while enjoying fascinating insights from an English-speaking chauffeur.

data.name: Via Crucis Catholic Pilgrim Tour in Rome
data.description: Embark on a spiritual experience like no other with the Via Crucis flagship Rome tour, an essential itinerary for Christian pilgrims to the heart of Christendom before and during the Holy Year.Created by and for traditional Catholics, the tour takes in the sacred Relics of Christ’s Passion, including part of the Holy Cross, the Holy Nails, the Crown of Thorns and the Title of the Cross, bearing the infamous inscription “Jesus the Nazarene, King of the Jews”. You'll also have the opportunity to see the Holy Stairs which Jesus climbed in condemnation, the pillar upon which He was scourged and other priceless artifacts from Christendom such as the Salus Popoli Romani icon by St. Luke and an example of Acheiropoieta in the Holy of Holies.This tour visits two of Rome's four Holy Doors along the way, at the Major Basilica of St. Mary Major and the Arch-Basilica of St. John Lateran, the Mother Church of the World. data.name: Ancient Rome: from the Capitoline Hill to the Colosseum along the Imperial Fora  – Private Tour
data.description: Your itinerary begins in Piazza del Campidoglio, one of Rome’s most scenic locations. Designed by Michelangelo and a symbol of the Renaissance, this square offers a perfect introduction to the sacred hill, home to Rome’s civic institutions and the famous Capitoline Museums. From here, we’ll descend toward the Via dei Fori Imperiali. As we stroll along this historic route, you’ll enjoy breathtaking views of the Roman Forum, the vibrant heart of ancient Rome, stretching out at the foot of the Capitoline Hill. Highlights include the remains of the Temple of Saturn, once the repository of the state treasury, and the Basilica Julia, a hub for legal and administrative affairs. Your guide will also delve into the significance of the Curia, the Senate's meeting hall, and the stories surrounding the imposing Arch of Septimius Severus, a monumental symbol of victory and imperial power. Continuing along the road, we’ll reach the Forum of Trajan, home to the exquisite Trajan’s Column, which narrates the emperor’s military campaigns through intricately carved reliefs. Just a short distance ahead, the Markets of Trajan stand as a remarkable testament to the commercial ingenuity of ancient Rome. These markets, considered precursors to modern shopping centers, were more than a simple marketplace. They served as the economic hub of the city, housing administrative offices, shops, and storage facilities, all ingeniously designed into the terraced slopes of the Quirinal Hill. A brief detour will take you to the picturesque Monti district, which in ancient times was the heart of the Suburra. It was the unhealthy and overcrowded “red-light” neighborhood, located just beyond the Fora where sub-proletarians and small traders lived. It was home to lupanari (ancient brothels) and notorious taverns, frequented by criminals, but also by aristocrats and matrons seeking forbidden thrills, and home to illustrious figures such as Julius Caesar and the poet Martial. The walk culminates at the awe-inspiring Colosseum, the ultimate symbol of Rome. Here, your guide will recount tales of gladiatorial battles, imperial festivities, and the grand spectacles that once captivated thousands. Even today, this iconic amphitheater enchants visitors from around the globe. This experience is perfect for those who wish to explore Rome at a leisurely pace, savoring every detail of an itinerary that spans more than two thousand years of history.

data.description: Just a few kilometres south of the splendid city of Naples, a marvellous peninsula bends towards the Mediterranean nuances of the Italian sea: the Amalfi Coast is such a charming and evocative place that it has been chosen by UNESCO as one of the most superlative examples of the majesty and luxury of Italian landscapes. Could we at Gray Line I Love Rome not think of all those who would love to discover this wonderful region with one of our most famous Day Trips? This is a region traditionally deeply connected to its sea, verdant landscapes and centuries-long history. Did you know that the beautiful Amalfi was one of the four Maritime Republics of Italy, together with Genoa, Pisa and Venice? Maritime Republics were independent city-states in Italy - during the Middle Ages – that had naval supremacy over a vast territory; they each had their own impressive fleet of ships for their protection, but also for large-scale trade networks across the Mediterranean basin. They were the bridge that connected the old European continent to the Middle East, to Africa and Asia, not only for trade purposes, but also cultural and artistic. During the golden years of the international jet set, in the 1960s, the Amalfi Coast was the favourite retreat for the most important international political, movies and show-biz personalities: from Jaqueline Kennedy to the Agnelli family, from Sophia Loren and Greta Garbo to Rudolf Nureyev. Among the most popular and visited destinations are Amalfi and Positano, included in this activity, but also Ravello, Procida and the spectacular Sorrento, that are definitely worth a few days’ trip. If you wish to become an expert of the region, ask our staff for all the other experiences: whether it is a day trip or a multi-day excursion, we guarantee you it will be unforgettable! This tour will allow you the chance to visit two of the most famous and popular villages of the Amalfi Coast: Amalfi and Positano. You will join a group of no more than 15 people, when meeting with your tour leader at the Roma Termini railway station to leave for Salerno onboard the high-speed train included in the package. Once in Salerno, you will reach Amalfi by ferryboat, which is truly the best way to explore the Coast and get the best possible view of the hills plunging into the sea, the coloured little houses and the majestic nature that surrounds you: you’ll feel like a movie star! Amalfi will be the first destination you reach: nestled in a ravine surrounded by stunning cliffs, it was known as the Duchy of Amalfi during the Middle Ages. Here you will have free time to explore the town, its public squares, shops and the Cathedral on your own. After visiting Amalfi, you will take the ferry back to Positano to discover all its charm and elegance: you will feel as if you ended up in a painting! Its coloured buildings, shops and sandy beaches will put a spell on you: visit the Marina Grande beach, just where the town meets the sea, or stroll around Fornillo or Arienzo beaches. data.name: Rome Underground Catacombs and Crypts
data.description: Important: Depending on different closing days, you will visit two catacombs between Domitilla’s, Saint Sebastian’s, Priscilla’s, San Callixtus's Catacombs. Discover the ancestral and underground area of Rome.You can admire several burial chambers and various pagan burial sites. These places were formerly used as burial grounds because it was forbidden to bury or cremate corpses in the city.  You can visit the largest and oldest underground cemetery in Rome. The catacombs of St. Callixtus were the official cemetery of the Church of Rome and half a million Christians were buried there among many martyrs and popes (the Crypt of the Popes). You will also admire the Crypt of St. Cecilia: the popular patron of music, she was martyred and entombed where the statue now lies.  Domitilla's catacombs are one of the most extensive catacombs in Rome, they are spread over 17 kilometers of underground caves, some of which are inaccessible, and they are situated over 16 meters underground. Some Christians have built these catacombs in the Ardeatina's area, after Domitilla had been banished in the III century. There are about 150000 burials, some of them are decorated. Saint Sebastian's catacombs, situated in Via Appia, are very important because historians believe that this place had hosted Saints Peter and Paul bodies. They are located in a slope that has always been used as a cemetery also before Christianism; later it was converted in a cemetery for slaves and freedmen.  Priscilla's catacombs are one of the most ancient underground cemetery. The first burials should go back to the second half of the II century AD and because of the big amount of graves in it, it is called "regina catacombarum". This cemetery was ransacked around the XVI century so there are no tombstones, coffins and tuff, nevertheless there are many well-preserved paintings.

data.name: Private Tiramisu and gelato-making class
data.description: Become a pastry chef for the day with us and learn how to make tiramisù and gelato from scratch during your Roman holiday: this 2-hour-class is suitable for foodies of any age and even for gluten and lactose intolerants. Reach our trusted local gourmet at our meeting point in the Campo De’ Fiori area and let the magic begin. In a group of 2 up to 10 people, you’ll learn everything about this lovely dessert: what to buy, how to bake ladyfingers, how to whip the perfect eggs and mascarpone cheese cream. You’ll work in a proper laboratory, inside a tiramisu shop, and a professional pastry chef will assist you all the time. Thanks to the step-by-step approach of this class, you’ll truly grasp the secrets and learn all the correct techniques that are required to make a perfect, creamy, luxurious tiramisu. During this class, you’ll also find out the actual difference between ice-cream and gelato, you’ll learn how to make sorbet, a delicious water-based fruit gelato, and...of course, there’ll be plenty of tastings during all the class, so don’t come on a full stomach! Afterward, you’ll receive the recipes, so you can show off your skills once you’re back home: don’t forget to post the pictures on your social media pages and tag us.

data.name: Audiencia Papal + Almuerzo + Museos Vaticanos
data.description: Experiencia Completa! En los museos vaticanos: Ingreso sin esperas - max. 15 personas Acerca de Por la mañana nuestra guia les acompañará a la Plaza San Pedro donde esperaremos el inicio de la Audiencia Papal (puede celebrarse en la Sala de Audiencias). Por la tarde, a las 14.00 h. nuestro guía se reunirá con Ud. en el restaurante y leo llevará a los Museos Vaticanos, para dar inicio a la visita de una de las colecciones de arte más ricas del mundo, para admirar, entre otros, la mundialmente conocida Capilla Sixtina, la obra maestra de Miguel Ángel. Desde los museos entraremos directamente a la Basílica de San Pedro, la más grande e importante Iglesia Católica del mundo, con sus tesoros como la escultura de Miguel Ángel La Piedad y el altar Baldaquín de Bernini. El tour finaliza en la Plaza San Pedro, dominada por la imponente cúpula de Miguel Ángel y rodeada por la famosa doble columnata del arquitecto Bernini. Duración 10 horas Idioma Inglés y español Incluye pase de admisión para la la Audiencia del Papa asistente por la mañana durante la Audiencia tiquets para saltar la cola de accesso a los Museos Vaticanos guía, auriculares almuerzo Punto de encuentro Via della Traspontina, 6 o servicio gratuito de recogida de hoteles céntricos. Final Plaza de San Pedro – traslados a los hoteles no esta incluido. IMPORTANTE: El Museo requiere que los clientes en silla de ruedas sigan un itinerario diferente y no estan autorizados permitido a realizar nuestro tour habitual. No es permitido entrar en la Iglesias en pantalón corto, hombros descubiertos, minifaldas. Esta asimismo prohibido entrar en el Museo con objetos de metal, paraguas y mochilas. Si la Basílica de San Pedro está cerrada para cerimonias religiosas,en sostitucion se visitará la Galeria de arte. Solo para la Audiencia Papal: el asistente o guía puede hablar en dos idiomas y e grupo puede se superior a 15 personas. El asiento durante la Audiencia Papal no está garantizado. Los tiquets de admisión para la Audiencia Papal son gratuítos.

data.name: IKONO Roma: Immersive Experience
data.description:
Step out of your comfort zone and dive into a unique experience you will never forget!

IKONO is the new immersive experience in the heart of Rome, just steps from the Pantheon.

Unleash your inner creativity in an exciting and unforgettable one-hour journey through nine surreal, and immersive exploration zones.

During your visit, you will interact with more than 12 never-seen-before interactive and artistic installations that combine sensory stimulation with cutting-edge technology.

Unlike traditional art galleries, in IKONO you're the real protagonist!

From the "Roman Thermae" with its giant ball pit to the "Tokyo Street" with its surreal atmosphere and exciting activities, IKONO Roma is an experience like no other.

This extraordinary adventure is suitable for people of all ages. The only requirement is to make each space yours! Are you ready to dive in?

Immerse yourself in the spectacular scenery without being held back by crowds or heat. Get ready for an unforgettable tour.

data.name: Rome Private Sightseeing Day Tour With Lunch and Pickup
data.description: Short on sightseeing time but long on Rome landmarks you want to check out? Tick a host of essential city sights, like the Colosseum and Trevi Fountain, from your bucket list with this private sightseeing tour. With lunch at a classic Roman joint and convenient round-trip hotel pickup included, the experience is even more seamless.

data.name: Rome Private Evening Golf Cart Tour, Aperitivo
data.description: Discover the magic of Rome at night with this private golf cart tour through the Eternal City. Starting at the historic Piazza della Repubblica, you’ll cruise past iconic landmarks like the Circus Maximus, the Aventine Hill with its stunning Orange Garden, and the enchanting Trevi Fountain. Along the way, indulge in Italian aperitivos, prosecco, craft beer, and local snacks as your guide shares stories of Rome’s rich history and culture.

data.name: Rome Squares Private Piazzas Walking Tour
data.description: Wander through Rome’s most iconic public squares on a private walking tour from Piazza Venezia to Piazza della Minerva. While many travelers rush through the piazzas en route to Rome’s more well-known landmarks, this immersive stroll takes in the beauty and history of the city’s favourite gathering spots. Explore grand fountains and tucked-away courtyards and learn about the role of piazzas in daily Roman life.

data.name: Barberini Palace & Galleria Corsini: Entry Ticket
data.description: Age before beauty? Not when it comes to art! See both combined at Palazzo Barberini, home to Renaissance highlights from Raphael, Caravaggio and more. See the frescoed ceiling, crucifixes and works by regional painters of popes and cardinals and get free access to Palazzo Corsini.

data.description: A step back to Medieval Tuscany!
